 Dated this the 16th day of April, 2024  ORDER
These bail applications are filed under Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code.

2. These bail applications are filed by one Rahila Banu M., who is arrayed as an accused in Crime Nos.99 of 2024, 100 of 2024, 97 of 2024, 108 of 2024, 114 of 2024, 140 of 2024, 139 of 2024, 153 of 2024 and 212 of 2024 of Nadakkavu Police Station.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code and also under Section 21 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (BUDS Act).

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (BUDS Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is one of the directors of the Company and she has no direct involvement in these cases.
It is also submitted that the petitioner has no authority to sign on behalf of the Company.
4. Heard the counsel for the petitioner and the public B.A.Nos.3007 of 2024 and Conn.Cases Prosecutor.
Learned Public Prosecutor seriously opposed the bail application.
5. After hearing both sides, I think this is not a fit case, in which orders u/s.438 Cr.P.C can be passed.

At this stage the counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner will surrender Rahila Banu M vs State Of Kerala on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99447521/
7 before the Investigating Officer.

entities.text: Rahila Banu M vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The counsel also submitted that there may be a direction to produce the petitioner after interrogation before the jurisdictional court and there may be a direction to the jurisdictional court to consider the bail application on the date of production of the petitioner.
I think that prayer can be allowed.
6. Considering the submission of the counsel for the petitioner, these bail applications are disposed of with the following directions.
i. The petitioner will surrender before the Investigating Officer within ten days from today.

ii. If the petitioner surrender before the Investigating Officer as directed above, the Investigating Officer is free to interrogate the petitioner and shall produce the petitioner before the jurisdictional court on the date of surrender itself.
B.A.Nos.3007 of 2024 and Conn.Cases iii.
The petitioner is free to file bail application before the jurisdictional court at the time of producing him before the Magistrate.

If such a bail application is filed with advance copy to the prosecutor concerned, the jurisdictional court will consider that bail application in accordance with law and pass appropriate orders in it preferably on the date of filing of the same itself.

iv. The Investigating Officer is free to file custody application, if necessary, at the time of producing the petitioner and if such application is filed, the jurisdictional court is free to pass appropriate orders in it also.

Sd/-
P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN, JUDGE ats Rahila Banu M vs State Of Kerala on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99447521/
